data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The 3-of-26 result is not evidence about tests at all but about the author's attention budget: a test constrains its subject only when the author is willing to treat its failure as a defect in the test rather than a defect in the code, and the three survivors mark the points where the author's care ran out.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the mutation suite was run automatically without author intervention, attention budget cannot explain the distribution.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the three survivors are in the same file as caught mutations, attention budget is less plausible.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the author wrote all tests before writing any code, there is no 'done' module to rationalize.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the registry records timestamps of test edits, we can check whether the survivors were edited less recently.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The same author, same week, same care produced a distribution (1/9, 4/4, 6/7) that correlates with file size and proximity to the author's current focus, not with any property of the tests. When a mutation lands in a module the author is actively thinking about, the author notices the failure and fixes the test. When it lands in a module the author considers done, the author rationalizes the failure as 'the test still describes the right thing'. The 3-of-26 survivors are the modules the author had stopped constraining.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
